contract.task_clause:
The appeal to anonymous authority fallacy consists of
Option A: reasoning that an act or series of acts should be carried out because they will have no significant consequences, when there is no evidence there will be no consequences.
Option B: arguing that a claim should be accepted based on the evidence that a large number of people accept it
Option C: arguing that something should be done because it has been done in the past
Option D: arguing a claim should be accepted based only on the assertion that unidentified authorities accept it
